newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu threatened over attorney general - paper.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu threatened over attorney general - paper.

text.p: A key witness told police that an Israeli politician used threats to force Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu into the ill-fated appointment of an attorney general last month, an Israeli newspaper said on Friday.

The witness, attorney Dan Avi-Yitzhak, resigned earlier this week from representing the head of the religious Shas party, Aryeh Deri, a figure at the heart of corruption allegations in the appointment of the attorney general.
Israel's Yedioth Ahronoth daily also said Netanyahu, in testimony he gave to police this week on the case, refrained from providing substantive answers to some questions.
Netanyahu's office refused to comment on the report as did police.
Israel's Haaretz daily said FBI Director Louis Freeh expressed an interest in the affair while in Israel this week, but it was not clear if Freeh was simply curious.

Other reports said the U.S. embassy was paying more attention to the case that has prompted some Israeli government ministers to say that even if a portion of the allegations proved to be true Netanyahu's government would have to go.
The U.S. embassy in Tel Aviv refused to comment on the reports. One diplomatic source said: "It's very usual for embassies to take note of what's happening".

Yedioth said lawyer Avi-Yitzhak in testimony that covered dozens of pages told police that "Deri threatened the prime minister...that if he did not appoint attorney Roni Bar-On to the post of attorney general he would make trouble for him."

Israeli radio stations reported that Avi-Yitzhak, who announced his resignation as Deri's defence lawyer on Wednesday, denied the Yedioth report. Avi-Yitzhak did not return calls made by Reuters to his office on Friday.

Deri has denied allegations -- first raised in an Israel television report -- that he pushed Bar-On's appointment in exchange for his Shas's support for the government's deal with the Palestinians for a partial troop withdrawal from the West Bank town of Hebron last month.
The television report said Bar-On promised Deri, on trial for the past three years on corruption charges, a plea bargain that would allow him to continue his political career.

Bar-On, a veteran activist in Netanyahu's Likud party, quit 12 hours after taking office last month amid allegations by jurists and politicians that he was a legal lightweight appointed only because of his loyalty to the prime minister.
Bar-On and Netanyahu have denied all allegations.
In the resignation letter to Deri leaked to the media and confirmed by Avi-Yitzhak, the attorney said:

"You have slandered me and my wife and spread lies about us and all because of my 'big sin' that I dared out of pure and relevant reasons to oppose your plan to appoint Roni Bar-On as the attorney-general and I did not succumb to your will."
Avi-Yitzhak was one of the candidates for the office of attorney-general but was passed up in favour of Bar-On.
Asked by Israel Radio about the alleged slander, Deri said: "That is a complete lie." As for the reference in Avi-Yitzhak's letter to Deri's "plan" to appoint Bar-On, Deri said:
"Look, this is under police investigation. What the letter said, that I had a plan to appoint Bar-On, is not true."
